title: Modular launch bundles for inference surface — PRD + readiness checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need a predictable, staged path to adopt the full Redwood inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) without a big-bang migration. This PRD defines modular "bundles" (minimal capability sets) that can be launched incrementally, with clear acceptance criteria, canary plan, and rollback controls. Goal: ship first two bundles (CoreGen: completions+chat minimal features; SearchLens: embeddings+rerank) and a dry-run migration guide for integrators.
requirements: Public REST/SDK endpoints for each bundle: /v1/bundles/coregen and /v1/bundles/searchlens
Schema-stable request/response contracts for chat and completions (including streaming and function-calls subset)
Embeddings API returns deterministic vector dims and clear normalization guidance
Reranker API accepts batching and returns score+explain for top-K results
Per-route quotas, billing labels and usage meters must be emitted for cost attribution
Region parity: us-west1 and eu-west1 for initial launch
Backward compatibility: existing hosted customers using legacy endpoints must keep behavior until opt-in migration
SDK updates (Python/Node) to expose bundle selection and compatibility helpers
Console items: per-bundle dashboard, latency/cost heatmap, rollout toggles
scope_changes: Initial scope planned CoreGen+SearchLens. During grooming we reduced full function-calls support to 'light mode' for wave-1 and deferred advanced structured-output validators to wave-2. Also trimmed multi-model routing UI from the launch scope: routing will use default policy with API config override only.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: CoreGen endpoints produce valid completions and chat responses for the provided conformance prompt set (suite v2.1) with no regressions vs control models
Performance: P95 token latency for short prompts (<64 tokens) <= 250ms in us-west1 on Dedicated-backed variant; cold-start first-token <= 350ms
Reliability: Error rate (5xx) for each bundle <= 0.2% over a 72h rolling window during canary
Compatibility: SDK integration tests (Python/Node) pass end-to-end against canary endpoints
Billing & Metering: Per-token and per-embedding metrics appear in usage logs and map to customer invoices in staging
Observability: Console dashboard shows per-route latency, cost breakdowns, and top failure types; tracing linkable to request IDs
Security: KMS integration validated for Private keys used in bundle config; security review completed
Operational: Canary runbook executed and rollback tested (see rollout_checklist item)
rollout_plan: Internal canary (team-only) for 48 hours: traffic limited to infra/qa tenants
Staged canary 1: 5% real traffic across low-risk customers for 72 hours; monitor P95 and 5xx
Staged canary 2: 25% traffic for 48 hours if metrics pass; enable cost telemetry and billing mapping
Open: 100% traffic and GA if metrics stable for 7 days; enable migration docs and auto-migration opt-in
Fallback: automatic rollback to legacy endpoint variant if error rate spikes >0.5% for 30m or P95 > 450ms for 30m
launch_checklist: Engineering: all E2E tests green in staging and production canary cluster
Engineering: SDK packages published to test PyPI/NPM tags and smoke-tests passed
Product: PRD sign-off and acceptance criteria verified
Design: API docs, quickstart, request/response examples for each bundle published
Console: dashboard widgets created and verified with synthetic traffic
Billing: usage events mapped to invoice metrics in staging ledger
Security: KMS/HSM keys validated for bundle config access; compliance checklist signed
Support: runbooks, triage playbooks, and knowledge base articles created
Customer success: migration plan and sample scripts for common SDKs ready
Legal: terms/TPA updates reviewed for new bundle feature set
Telemetry: tracing ID correlated across services and sampling configured
Chaos: rollback tested via simulated infra failure during canary
monitoring_and_alerts: Create per-bundle SLA dashboards (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate)
Alerts: p95 latency > 350ms for 15m -> paging to SRE
Alerts: error rate (5xx) > 0.5% for 10m -> SD escalation
Cost alert: per-customer per-bundle daily spend > threshold -> notify finance & account owner
Tracing: missing correlation headers flagged as high-priority logs for dev investigation
regression_tests: Conformance suite: representative prompts for completions/chat/embeddings/rerank (v2.1)
SDK compatibility matrix: Node 16+, Python 3.9+ smoke-tests
Performance automation: replay 10k synthetic requests with realistic sequence length distributions
Billing validation: end-to-end invoice test for sample tenant using staging ledger
dependencies: SEC-9001: KMS integration for hosted bundle configs
decisions: Decision: Wave-1 will ship light function-calls support (only single-function sync pattern). Rationale: function-calls full graph postponed to reduce runtime surface risk.
Decision: Use billing label 'bundle_coregen' and 'bundle_searchlens' for quick cost mapping.
Decision: Defer multi-model routing UI; expose routing config via API only for initial launch.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected latency regressions when enabling prefix-level KV caching for chat. Mitigation: enable cache by config flag and test with synthetic workload; if regressions occur, revert flag in canary cluster.
Risk: Billing mismatch between usage logs and invoice rendering. Mitigation: end-to-end invoice test and manual reconciliation during canary.
Risk: Customers misinterpret bundle semantics. Mitigation: publish clear migration guide and provide CS-led onboarding for early adopters.
metrics_and_sla: SLO: p95 token latency <= 300ms (GA objective) per bundle
SLO: availability >= 99.9% per bundle per region
Metric: cost-per-1k-tokens (observed) reported daily for each bundle
Metric: embed-dim consistency failure rate must be <0.01%
notes: This PRD is intentionally conservative: bundle concept reduces surface risk for customers and lets us iterate on complex features (structured output, advanced function-calls, routing UI) in subsequent waves. Track all scope reductions explicitly and attach deferred work as child PM tickets.
follow_up_actions: Create PM child issues for wave-2 features (advanced function-calls, structured validators)
Schedule cross-functional GA readiness review two working days before target GA
Coordinate with SRE for a load-test window and post-launch review
